headline: Boiler explosion leads to fire at Gazipur oil factory
summary: The blaze at Auto Green Oil Company was brought under control by three firefighting units after nearly an hour of effort.
details: A fire broke out at the Auto Green Oil Company in the College Gate (Maijgaon) area under Pubail Police Station in Gazipur following a boiler explosion this afternoon.
The blaze erupted around 2:10 pm and was brought completely under control by 3:00 pm through the efforts of three firefighting units from the Tongi Fire Service and Civil Defence Station.
Senior station officer Md Shahin Alam stated that the facility was operating illegally and posed significant safety risks, as it burned discarded tyres to produce unrefined fuel for sale.
Fire service officials reported that no company representatives were found at the scene, and the owner of the company allegedly fled after learning about the fire.
A detailed investigation is currently underway to ascertain the exact cause of the fire and the total amount of damage incurred.
caption:

Senior station officer Md Shahin Alam stated that the facility was operating illegally and posed significant safety risks, as it burned discarded tyres to produce unrefined fuel for sale.

Fire service officials reported that no company representatives were found at the scene, and the owner of the company allegedly fled after learning about the fire.

A detailed investigation is currently underway to ascertain the exact cause of the fire and the total amount of damage incurred.

headline_marked: Editors' Council [[demands release of jailed editor]] over news report
headline: Editors' Council demands release of jailed editor over news report
summary: The organization condemned the arrest of Md Rezanur Islam, acting editor of daily Agrajatra Pratidin, calling it an 'alarming repetition' of past harassment of journalists.
details: The Editors' Council has expressed deep concern and strong condemnation over the arrest and imprisonment of Md Rezanur Islam, acting editor of daily Agrajatra Pratidin, following a published news report.
Rezanur was arrested by the Detective Branch (DB) of Bogura district police from his residence in Gazipur's Joydebpur area on Thursday night.

The arrest follows a case filed under the Cyber Security Act, which includes extortion charges, for allegedly spreading propaganda and defamatory information involving LGRD State Minister Mir Shahe Alam.
The Editors' Council termed the arrest an 'alarming repetition' of the lawsuits and harassment journalists faced during the previous Awami League regime.
The council stated that the incident contradicts the BNP's election manifesto and its 31-point state reform pledge regarding media freedom.
They noted that if anyone is aggrieved by a news report, they should seek recourse through the Press Council or existing laws rather than arresting journalists.
The statement highlighted that Bangladesh currently ranks 152nd in the World Press Freedom Index, and such arrests further degrade media freedom and the country's image abroad.
When produced before a court yesterday afternoon, Chief Judicial Magistrate Abdullah Al Mamun sent Rezanur to jail.
Meanwhile, LGRD State Minister Mir Shahe Alam has issued a statement clarifying that he did not give any approval or directive to file the case.
caption:
A journalist is in jail over a news report. The Editors' Council calls it an 'alarming repetition' of past harassment.

The Editors' Council has expressed deep concern and strong condemnation over the arrest and imprisonment of Md Rezanur Islam, acting editor of daily Agrajatra Pratidin, following a published news report.

Rezanur was arrested by the Detective Branch (DB) of Bogura district police from his residence in Gazipur's Joydebpur area on Thursday night.

The arrest follows a case filed under the Cyber Security Act, which includes extortion charges, for allegedly spreading propaganda and defamatory information involving LGRD State Minister Mir Shahe Alam.

The Editors' Council termed the arrest an 'alarming repetition' of the lawsuits and harassment journalists faced during the previous Awami League regime.

The council stated that the incident contradicts the BNP's election manifesto and its 31-point state reform pledge regarding media freedom.

They noted that if anyone is aggrieved by a news report, they should seek recourse through the Press Council or existing laws rather than arresting journalists.

The statement highlighted that Bangladesh currently ranks 152nd in the World Press Freedom Index, and such arrests further degrade media freedom and the country's image abroad.

When produced before a court yesterday afternoon, Chief Judicial Magistrate Abdullah Al Mamun sent Rezanur to jail.

Meanwhile, LGRD State Minister Mir Shahe Alam has issued a statement clarifying that he did not give any approval or directive to file the case.
